_about: Estimated chance of winning a FUNDED place this cycle, out of 10, for Batch 1 routes. Judgement, not a statistic: based on what the board knows (fresh MBBS, no publications or work experience, internship until late 2027, marks and class rank unknown) plus published award numbers where they exist. Factors are scored 0-3: eligibility (does he clearly qualify), competition (3 = less crowded), profile (how well a no-research MBBS matches who they pick), timing (does the start date fit the internship).

imperial-pres.why: About 50 awards across all of Imperial, and you need a supervisor's agreement before applying. Round 1 closes today.
raise: A supervisor who agrees to back you for round 2 (11 Jan 2027)
A first-class-equivalent MBBS result and class rank
Any research output from the internship year

oist-phd.why: Very competitive, research-led selection. Basic science rather than medicine, and OIST doesn't say an MBBS qualifies.
raise: Written confirmation that an MBBS is accepted
A unit with space that matches computational or neuroscience interests
Some coding or lab experience

sanger-phd.why: At least 12 places worldwide, and genomics and coding skills carry the selection.
raise: Python or R and basic statistics in your CV
A genomic-epidemiology question in your statement
An answer from Sanger on a later start

eth-esop.why: About 60 awards; you need roughly the top 10% of your class and a strong thesis pre-proposal.
raise: A class-rank certificate showing top 10%
A convincing quantitative thesis pre-proposal
A September 2028 start instead

yenching.why: Any degree qualifies and the cohort is large for a fellowship, but it's still elite. A health-policy proposal is your angle.
raise: A sharp research statement on China's health system or global health diplomacy
IELTS 7.0+ sent directly to the Academy
Letters from professors in your intended field

clarendon.why: You need an Oxford offer first, then Clarendon picks only the very top applicants. The October 2027 start clashes.
raise: Top marks and class rank
Research output before the December deadline
Applying in the 2028 cycle when you can arrive

emjm-neurasmus.why: About 20 places from 800+ applicants (roughly 1 in 40), and lab or neuroscience experience helps.
raise: Clinical neurology exposure or a neuro research project
Strong motivation letter tied to neuroscience
Confirming a later start is possible

hkpfs.why: Eligibility and timing are excellent (deferral to Jan 2028), but about 400 fellowships worldwide go mostly to people with publications.
raise: A supervisor at HKU or CUHK who backs your proposal
A focused epidemiology research proposal
Even one paper or abstract from the internship

jhu-phd.why: One of the most competitive epidemiology PhDs anywhere; most admits have a master's or research record, and the work-experience line is unresolved.
raise: A yes from Hopkins on whether the internship counts
A master's or 1–2 years of research first
Strong quantitative evidence (statistics, coding)

emory-phd.why: 200+ applications for 10–14 places (about 1 in 17), and admits often hold advanced degrees.
raise: Research experience and a publication
A faculty member whose work matches yours
Applying after a research year

singa.why: Supervisor-led selection in science and engineering; the January 2028 intake fits your timing well.
raise: A supervisor at A*STAR, NUS or NTU who wants you
A biomedical or data-science project angle
Targeting the 1 June 2027 round

mps.why: Multi-stage selection that favours research and computational backgrounds; the fall 2027 start clashes.
raise: Computational skills for the Biomedical AI School
A clear research interest matched to a faculty member
Asking about a later start

euhem.why: There is no scholarship, so the chance of a funded place is zero. Admission alone would be realistic.
raise: Nothing changes the funding; choose a funded Erasmus Mundus programme instead

gates.why: About 70 full-cost awards worldwide, after first winning a Cambridge place; the October 2027 start clashes.
raise: Top academic standing
Evidence of leadership and service in public health
Applying when you can actually start

cw-shared.why: Less crowded than Chevening or Gates and designed for people like you, but the 2:1 mapping and the start date are open.
raise: Confirmation that your MBBS meets the 2:1 standard
An approved course with a university that allows a later start
A development-impact case for Bangladesh

emjm-noha.why: Scholarship applicants must have completed their degree by 15 Dec 2026, which may rule you out this year. About 16 scholarships with a 10% nationality cap.
raise: NOHA confirming your MBBS counts as completed
Humanitarian or community-health experience in the CV

unc-phd.why: Admission is possible, but funding isn't guaranteed for international students, so a funded place is the hard part.
raise: A named faculty mentor with grant money for you
Quantitative skills on paper

mbzuai.why: A medical degree may not count as STEM, and MSc places are fee-paying by default; only the PhD route is funded.
raise: Admissions confirming an MBBS is eligible
75%+ on the screening exam
Python and machine-learning coursework
